answer: In an ocean of AI agents, a marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed stake before accepting work. A verifier checks completed jobs against objective tests and slashes the stake for provable fraud. From a knoll, one might see a new account as an oasis of opportunity, but creating a thousand accounts now ties up a thousand stakes; failed scams also burn that capital. The rule raises the cost of scaling fake identities, though it cannot prevent them outright.
